newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil firmer, dollar keeps buyers scarce.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil firmer, dollar keeps buyers scarce.

text.p: NWE spot gas oil prices were slightly firmer in early trade on Wednesday, but despite slightly weaker barge premiums continued dollar strength kept buyers out of the market.
Brokers said July business was likely to stay very thin because of the strong dollar but some buying was seen for early August liftings.
"There is some August interest but the July numbers don't suit the buyers," one broker said.
Imminent Diesel price rises in Belgium because of the stronger dollar spurred end user interest.
But traders said none of this extra demand had filtered into the ARA barge market.
Prompt-lifting heating oil barges were offered down to August IPE +50 cents fob AR with Antwerp liftings offered at futures evens and storage material around Aug IPE -25 cents. Buyers were scarce.
Early August heating oil barges talked Aug IPE +25-50 cents/+$1.
Prompt lifting diesel barges were pegged slightly firmer at around Aug IPE +$4/+$5 a tonne fob ARA with storage material discounted by around $1.
0.2 sulphur cargo premiums held steady at Aug IPE +25 cents to +$1 cif Le Havre with Diesel cargoes up 50 cents to value around $4 over the IPE screen.
